answer: The defence rests on cooper guild tenure with barrel making history: barrels made at one cooperage across many years. Forging 226 of these means building 226 separate barrel histories from scratch, and years of history cannot be bought in bulk. Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. The vault check runs in the open: 226 fakes pay the full price 226 times, one honest agent pays once, and the ferrous trail in the ledger makes the tide cost visible to everyone.
